promptAsSent:
Use the image_gen tool to generate exactly one image, then stop. Do not write files, run commands or edit anything.

Attached reference images, in order:
Image 1: Geometry authority: exact silhouettes, layout, placement, scale and heading; flat colours are placeholders, not material
Image 2: Approved design concept: panelling, parts and detailing of the low-tech, midline and high-tech drones; not layout, heading or scale
Image 3: Rendering style and detail level only; not layout, palette, shape or subject
Image 4: Low-tech livery and material reference only; not layout, pose, shape or scale
Image 5: Midline livery and material reference only; not layout, pose, shape or scale
Image 6: High-tech livery and material reference only; not layout, pose, shape or scale

Paint image 1, a flat-colour geometry guide, as a sheet of three finished top-down game sprites of the same small hovering robotic DRONE unit for a science-fiction strategy game, about a metre long, launched from a ground drone station and carrying one forward barrel housing, as three spacefaring factions build it. None uses a fan; each is held up by thrust jets or vents. The bottom-right panel of the guide is empty: leave it empty.
- top-left, LOW-TECH: a blunt slab-sided armoured box of riveted pressed steel with a stubby barrel on a bolted mount, held up by two downward jet lift pods on short outrigger arms, with scorched nozzle rims and worn hazard-yellow striping; crude, overbuilt frontier kit. Image 4 is its livery and material reference.
- top-right, MIDLINE: a practical angular armoured pod in grey and muted slate blue with a small turret forward and a short barrel, lift from four flush slotted belly thrust grilles at the corners; toolbox utility. Image 5 is its livery and material reference.
- bottom-left, HIGH-TECH: a narrow pearl-white lifting body with an emitter tube on its centreline and a cyan lens, two swept edge fins, gravitic lift shown only as a thin cyan edge glow; corporate precision. Image 6 is its livery and material reference.
Image 2 is the approved concept for these drones (the LOW-TECH, MIDLINE and HIGH-TECH ones): follow its panelling, parts and detailing, but the guide's outline, size and heading win wherever they differ. Images 4 to 6 are livery and material only, never shape or layout.
Strict 90-degree overhead orthographic view, no perspective tilt, lit from the upper left. Every drone faces LEFT (nose toward the left edge), exactly where the guide puts it, at exactly the guide's size, position and outline; never move, rotate, rescale or recompose anything, add nothing between the drones and leave any empty guide panel empty. In the guide, flat colours only say what each region is: pale grey is hull plating, mid grey is structure, frames and fins, near-black bars are barrels and emitter tubes, dark slate blocks are thrust nozzle cowls, cyan marks soft cyan lights, lenses and exhaust glow, dark navy is sensor glass.
BANNED SHAPES, never draw any of these: fans, fan blades, rotors, rotor rings or discs, propellers, ducted props, round ducts or grilles over round ducts, quadcopter arms. These drones fly on thrust nozzles and vents only.
Rendered as finished top-down game sprites matching the rendering scale and level of detail of the attached approved vehicle sprite (rendering style only, not layout, palette or subject): grounded, believable, subtly weathered, crisp and readable when shrunk to 40 pixels, not glossy concept art. True transparent background with genuine alpha outside every silhouette, including gaps between fins, antenna blades, pods and body; no ground, scene, cast-shadow slab, labels, text, border, grid or checkerboard. Same square canvas as the guide.
